result.title: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Before Post-Training: An End-to-End Approach
result.summary: Agentic capabilities are increasingly important for modern LLMs, yet remain difficult to evaluate during pretraining. Existing approaches typically rely on static trajectory-derived tasks or likelihood-based proxies, which are lightweight but provide limited visibility into how base models behave in interactive environments. We introduce ASAP (Agent Scaffold Adaptation for Pretraining Evaluation), a lightweight framework for eliciting and evaluating agentic behavior from pretrained base models on end-to-end tasks. Rather than converting base models into chat-style agents, ASAP preserves the completion interface and adapts existing agent scaffolds through structured trajectory continuation, short reference prefixes, and minimal recovery mechanisms. Across software-engineering and deep-research benchmarks, ASAP yields discriminative end-to-end performance across base models and pretraining checkpoints. Beyond aggregate scores, ASAP exposes model-generated execution trajectories, enabling analysis of exploration, editing, testing, recovery, and task completion across training stages. These trajectories provide a behavioral view of how agent-relevant capabilities change during pretraining and how execution patterns differ after post-training. Our results suggest that end-to-end agent evaluation can complement conventional pretraining benchmarks by providing a practical diagnostic of interactive model behavior.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ASAP 框架：不把预训练基座模型改造成对话式 agent，而是保留补全接口，通过结构化轨迹延续、短参考前缀与最小恢复机制，在软件工程和深度研究基准上端到端引出并评测各预训练检查点的 agent 行为。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不改接口、用轨迹延续与短前缀引出行为」的做法，可能可供核查如何在不改变生成形式的前提下引出并观察模型的探索、恢复与终止行为，与 LVR 推理状态的使用和评价有间接方法联系；但论文面向纯文本 agent 评测，与视觉 latent 推理无直接关系。
